title: The angels
hook: created from light, obeying, never tiring

segments.voice: Yesterday, Allah, the One, and your line: one. Four short verses, worth a third of the Qur'an.

Watch the end of any Muslim prayer. The person sitting on the floor turns the head to the right and says peace be upon you, and the mercy of Allah. Then to the left, the same words. In a row, there's a person on each side, so the greeting lands somewhere. But some scholars say it's meant for more than the neighbors: it's also for the angels, the ones the Qur'an describes as noble recorders, keeping watch over every person. A small turn of the head, and a hello to the second article of faith.
screen: `RIGHT, THEN LEFT.` → `PEACE BE UPON YOU.` → `TO WHOM?`

segments.voice: Day six hundred sixty-five met the angels by name; today, why they're an article of faith. Start with what they're made of. A hadith in Sahih Muslim says the angels were created from light, the jinn from smokeless fire, and Adam from what you have been told: the earth. Three kinds of creature, three materials. Next, what they do. The Qur'an describes angels who carry out what they're commanded and do not disobey, and others who glorify Allah night and day without tiring. Some are known by name and task: Jibril, who brought the revelation, Mika'il, and the angel of death. Others record, others guard. Then a surprise. Obedient doesn't mean silent. In the second surah, Allah tells the angels, in Pickthall's translation, "Lo! I am about to place a viceroy in the earth." And the angels ask: will you put there someone who will do harm and shed blood, when we praise you? Allah answers that He knows what they don't. Adam is taught the names of things, and the angels admit they know only what they've been taught. The beings of light ask, and then they learn. Last, why believe in them at all. For Muslims, angels are part of how the unseen world works: revelation came through one, deeds are written by others, and no deed goes unwitnessed. That's held not as a mood but as the second of the six.
screen: `LIGHT, FIRE, EARTH.` · `THEY OBEY AND DON'T TIRE.` · `THE ANGELS ASKED A QUESTION.` · then, large: `NO DEED UNWITNESSED.`

segments.voice: Settle, then turn your head gently to the right and say, aloud or inside, peace be upon you; turn to the left and say it again. Then face forward and stay there. If you pray, this is the greeting you already know; if you don't, take it as a greeting to whatever company you keep, the people near you and whatever is unseen.
The angels. Mala'ikah in Arabic: created from light, obeying their Lord, glorifying Him without tiring. The second article of faith. Today's word.
Your line: made of light. Tomorrow, the third article of faith: the books. See you tomorrow, then.

howItsDone: Muslims end each prayer by turning the head right and left with the words peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah; belief in angels, including Jibril and the recording angels, is the second article of faith.

trapdoor: what you thought: angels are winged babies on greeting cards.
what it means: in Islam, angels are beings of light who carry out Allah's commands: bringing revelation, recording deeds, guarding.
what a scholar hears: the hadith of the three materials, the angels' question in Surah al-Baqarah, and the discussion of whom the closing salam of prayer addresses.

chat.says: Do Muslims think angels just obey, or can they ask questions?
options: They obey, yet in surah two they ask Allah a question, and then they learn.
They can't speak at all; angels only act and never say a word.
They only sing praise; the Qur'an never shows them speaking with Allah.
chat.meaning: In surah two the angels ask why Allah would place a viceroy on earth; He answers, and they admit they know only what they've been taught.
